name: Fishing Port
hero_subtitle: A working Atlantic harbour of blue boats, nets and the day’s catch — Essaouira’s most vivid morning scene.

overview.title: Blue hulls and morning catch
overview.p1: Essaouira’s fishing port is still a workplace: painted boats, drying nets and the rhythm of vessels leaving and returning. It is one of the most honest and photogenic corners of town.
overview.p2: Come in the morning for energy. Stay clear of restricted zones and ask before close photos of workers. Grilled fish nearby is the natural follow-up.
overview.p3: The port sits against the medina walls, so it slots easily between a Skala walk and an afternoon on the beach.

food.title: Food at the Fishing Port
food.p1: This is the place for simple grilled fish — agree the price before cooking at informal stalls.
food.li1: Choose a stall and agree the price first.
food.li2: Sardines and seasonal catch are common.
food.li3: Medina restaurants if you prefer a table inland.
food.p2: Keep expectations rustic; the charm is the setting.

tips.title: Practical tips for the Fishing Port

1.title: Access
1.desc: Open walkways around the harbour; avoid marked work areas.

2.title: Wind & sun
2.desc: Channel wind is constant — a light jacket helps.

3.title: Respect
3.desc: Ask before portraits; give way to fishers and carts.

q1.question: Can I walk freely?
q1.answer: On public edges yes; respect barriers and working crew.

q2.question: Best time?
q2.answer: Morning when boats and markets are most active.

q3.question: Where to eat the catch?
q3.answer: Informal grill stalls line parts of the quay — agree prices first.

q4.question: Good for photos?
q4.answer: Yes — blue hulls and harbour light are classic Essaouira shots.

q5.question: Safe with children?
q5.answer: Yes on the main walkways; hold hands near the water edge.
